messages.content: Could you provide me with the hourly forecast for temperature, wind speed, and precipitation for the next 10 days at the coordinates 37.8651 N, 119.5383 W?

function.name: fetch_weather_data
function.description: Retrieves weather forecast data for a specific location using the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The API endpoint for fetching weather data. This should be the full URL, including protocol and domain, without parameters.

latitude.description: The latitude of the location for which weather data is to be fetched. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: The longitude of the location for which weather data is to be fetched. This is a float type value.

units.description: The units for temperature and wind speed.

language.description: The language for weather condition texts.

message.reasoning:
We need to call fetch_weather_data function. Provide URL default. Provide latitude 37.8651, longitude -119.5383. Units metric. Language en. Also need hourly forecast for next 10 days. The API supports hourly parameters. We need to specify parameters? The function signature doesn't include parameters. But we can pass them via URL? The function expects url only. But we can include query parameters in the URL. So we need to construct full URL with parameters: hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability? Actually precipitation. The API uses precipitation_sum or precipitation_probability. For precipitation amount use precipitation_sum. So hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_sum. Also we need timezone. Use timezone=auto. Also start and end? The API returns up to 7 days by default? Actually open-meteo supports up to 7 days for free. But we need 10 days. Might need to use "forecast_days=10". The API supports forecast_days parameter. So include forecast_days=10. So URL: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_sum&forecast_days=10&timezone=auto&units=metric. But units param is separate? Actually units is part of query: &temperature_unit=metric? Wait open-meteo uses "temperature_unit=metric" and "windspeed_unit=kmh" etc. But we can just rely on default metric. So we can omit units. We'll include timezone=auto.

Thus call function.
